title: പള്ളിയിൽ നിന്ന് ബഹിരാകാശത്തേക്ക് 🚀⛪ ബിഷപ്പ് "പറ്റില്ല" പറഞ്ഞിരുന്നെങ്കിലോ? #shorts
description:
1963-ൽ തുമ്പയിലെ സെന്റ് മേരി മഗ്ദലീൻ പള്ളി ഇന്ത്യയുടെ ആദ്യ റോക്കറ്റിന് വഴിമാറി. ഒരു ഞായറാഴ്ച കുർബാനയ്ക്കിടെ ബിഷപ്പ് ചോദിച്ചു, മത്സ്യത്തൊഴിലാളികൾ "ആമേൻ" പറഞ്ഞു. ബിഷപ്പ് "പറ്റില്ല" പറഞ്ഞിരുന്നെങ്കിലോ?

India's first sounding rocket, a two-stage NASA-supplied Nike-Apache, lifted off from Thumba near Thiruvananthapuram on 21 November 1963 at about 6:25 pm and released a sodium vapour cloud that glowed orange in the dusk. Thumba was chosen because it lies close to Earth's magnetic equator. Vikram Sarabhai met Bishop Peter Bernard Pereira on a Saturday; at the next day's mass the bishop asked his parish to give up the church, and, in A.P.J. Abdul Kalam's account, got a hearty 'Amen'. The prayer room became the scientists' first lab, the bishop's house became the design office, and 183 families moved to a new church at Pallithura. The church has been the VSSC Space Museum since 1985.

Characters are friendly cartoon caricatures. The 'hungry country' line is a dramatised version of a common criticism, and the 'what if' is our own thought experiment. Some accounts say the first rockets were assembled in a nearby school building.

Sources: ISRO (diamond jubilee of the first sounding rocket launch, Nov 2023), Wikipedia (TERLS), Onmanorama (quoting Kalam's Ignited Minds), ThePrint/PTI (Aug 2023), The Better India (Nov 2016).
